name: pose-drag
about: The bone rig's baseline, and what puppet pins are compared against (Q239): on a rigged character, take the Bone tool, switch to posing, and swing the wrist through a wide arc twice, then undo both. Each drag is 1.5 s at 120 events a second. Measures the UI cost of each pointer batch while posing (pose.drag), building the posed drawing's geometry (pose.frame — evaluate, solve, densify and blend, before a dab is stamped), re-stamping it (the cache-miss frame span the lab already reads), how long the moved drawing took to reach the screen, and the key written on release (pose.commit). The fixture's arm lies along the middle of the document: shoulder at [0.35, 0.5], elbow at [0.5, 0.5], wrist at [0.65, 0.5]; the drag starts on the wrist tip. Run it against --fixture rigged-heavy to see what a painted character costs rather than an inked one.
